title: Neighbour holds barbecue to help stabbing victim's family
article: Clive Stewart didn't know the woman who was stabbed to death in his Jane Street and Sheppard Avenue townhouse complex last month, but felt compelled to do something to help the grieving family.

"I mentioned to my neighbour that we needed to do something so we went around the community and printed flyers out for a fundraiser barbecue," Stewart said, adding the June 4 barbecue raised $700, which was given to Pandora Whyte's family to help with funeral costs.
Whyte, 62, was fatally stabbed May 27 inside her townhouse.
The 34-year-old suspect, Ucal Lauzon, was shot to death during a confrontation with a police officer who responded to a disturbance call at 1898 Sheppard Ave. near Jane Street.

"Stuff is going on in the area," Stewart said of the crime that has plagued the area. "There is gang stuff going on. The kids have nothing to do. I have three kids and I have to think of my family and I don't want to see my son walk out there and something happens to him. The kids have nothing to do so they take up violence."
The Brady Crescent resident said various grocery stores donated hot dogs, hamburgers, chicken and drinks for the barbecue, which drew a large crowd, including 31 Division officers.
Although violence is a regular occurrence in his neighbourhood, Stewart said Whyte's murder came as a shock.

"My niece said big stuff was going on outside but I thought it was some youths," he recalled of the tragic night. "I thought, I have to have a fundraiser for these people. And if something like this happens again, I would do it again."
